subject: MSA/Order Form: SCCs scope, processor-role mapping, and transfer-impact addendum (TIA) escalation
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@novasys.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: legal@novasys.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form — SCCs and TIA follow-up

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form earlier. Our legal team reviewed the DPA exhibits and flagged two potential blockers: (1) the proposed SCCs mapping in Exhibit B currently lists Redwood as a controller for select telemetry which we believe should remain processor-only; and (2) Novasys requires an explicit transfer-impact addendum for EU-origin data routing to our US analytics subprocessor — their compliance lead marked this as a gating item for procurement.

I attached Novasys' suggested redline (Novasys_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a short note on the SCCs exception they might accept (SCCs-exception-proposal.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

- Reclassify the telemetry described in Exhibit B to "processor-only" handling (we've highlighted the clauses), and
- Accept a TIA template that binds routing restrictions with an audit window?

If this is something your legal/ops team needs to escalate internally, please let us know the earliest possible ETA — procurement has a tight sprint this week.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Contracts, Novasys

-----
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@novasys.com>, Novasys Legal <legal@novasys.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft MSA & Order Form — SCCs and TIA follow-up

Team — forwarding Novasys' redlines and ask. High level: they want two changes that could impact our standard SCCs posture and order-form ops.

Key asks from Novasys:
- Move specific telemetry items in Exhibit B to "processor-only" scope (see highlights) — this affects our ability to route/derive metrics in US analytics.
- Sign a TIA that restricts cross-border routing for EU-origin data to a named subprocessor list and mandates an annual audit window.

Ben — this is a deal blocker if procurement can't sign this week. Can you coordinate with Solutions to see if we have flexibility on the telemetry carveout?
Karthik — legal: initial read on SCCs exception and whether we can accept a TIA with the proposed audit language without a broader change to our risk posture.
Laura — ops/timing: what's the lift if we carve routing controls into a TIA for this account?

I'll keep Novasys in the loop but want an internal decision first.

Eve

-----
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MSA & Order Form — SCCs and TIA follow-up

Eve — quick update after sync with solutions and product:

- Telemetry: the metrics they want to exclude are operational logs and usage counters we currently use for batching heuristics. We can create a separate collection pipeline for EU-origin telemetry that excludes identifiers used in analytics, which would satisfy a processor-only promise. That requires a short configuration change in our ingest layer (estimate 2 sprints) and an operating playbook to ensure no commingling.
- TIA: product can support a named-subprocessor routing restriction and export an audit log, but the audit window language needs to be narrow — we can offer quarterly attestation + one annual SOC snapshot rather than an open-ended "audit anytime" clause.

Ask: can legal accept the narrower audit language? If so, I can communicate the workaround to Novasys and request a non-blocking procurement ETA.

Attaching a proposed TIA draft I asked Solutions to sketch: TIA-draft-20260519.docx

Ben
Account Executive

-----
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MSA & Order Form — SCCs and TIA follow-up

Eve/Ben — legal review notes (high level):

1) SCCs role mapping: We need to be careful with language that broadly labels telemetry as processor-only. SCCs mapping is a factual exercise: for each processing activity we must document whether Redwood acts as controller or processor. If we accept their proposed carveout, we should add a tied clause that limits our obligations to non-product-analytics telemetry and explicitly preserves Redwood's right to use aggregated non-identifiable metrics.

2) TIA / audit scope: "Audit anytime" is not acceptable operationally. Proposed compromise — allow Novasys to request an independent third-party attestation once per year (scope narrowly defined to routing controls and subprocessor list), plus the standard SOC snapshot. We should push back on "ad-hoc forensic access" and instead offer incident-triggered deeper review subject to NDAs and mutual scoping.

3) Order Form redlines: Any change that affects data routing must be captured in the order form via an exhibit, not only in the DPA, so procurement and ops have clear obligations post-signature. Suggest we: (a) accept the narrowed TIA language; (b) update Exhibit B to list the excluded telemetry fields; and (c) include an ops runbook reference (internal link) describing the separation mechanism.

I'll draft redline language for the MSA/DPA if you want me to propose final wording.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Privacy

-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MSA & Order Form — SCCs and TIA follow-up

Folks — ops feasibility note:

- Implementing the EU-only telemetry pipeline (segregation) is feasible but will require a short scoping sprint and a one-time config change in routing (we can prioritize for this customer). No infra-level refactor required.
- Audit support: we can provide quarterly attestation exports and a yearly audit package (logs + configs) for a narrow scope. For any third-party audit, we'd need at least 30 days notice and a defined playbook; red team or ad-hoc forensic access is a no-go.
- Timeline: if we sign the narrowed TIA today, we can deliver routing controls and attestation within 6 business days for go-live, full runbook and documentation in 3 weeks.

I'll coordinate with Product and Ops to produce the runbook and the exhibit language once legal confirms.

Laura
Director, Product Ops

-----
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@novasys.com>, Novasys Legal <legal@novasys.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form — SCCs and TIA follow-up

Samantha / Marcus,

Thanks for the quick flag — we reviewed internally and have a proposed path forward:

1) Redwood accepts reclassifying the identified telemetry fields as processor-only for Novasys EU-origin traffic, documented in Exhibit B (we will provide exact clause language).
2) For the TIA: Redwood will sign a transfer-impact addendum limited to routing controls and subprocessor list, offering quarterly attestation exports and one annual independent attestation (scope: routing controls + subprocessor confirmations). Any additional third-party audit requests will require 30 days' notice and mutual scoping (NDA in place).
3) Operations will implement an EU-origin telemetry segregation and deliver the runbook within 3 weeks; we can enable the production control within 6 business days to avoid blocking procurement.

Karthik will circulate the proposed contract redlines (MSA/DPA/Exhibit B) by EOD today. Ben will update Novasys procurement with the ETA and TIA summary. Laura and Product Ops will own the runbook and attestations.

Samantha — if that aligns with Novasys' procurement gating criteria, please confirm and we will share the redline package and the TIA doc for signature.

Regards,
Eve
Senior Manager, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: Novasys_MSA_redline_v3.docx; SCCs-exception-proposal.pdf; TIA-draft-20260519.docx]
